suggestions: pre-filter a large table as a CTE before the join
reorder joins to reduce intermediate rows
convert an IN subquery to a semi-join
reached_sql:
WITH filtered_items AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk, i_brand_id, i_brand
    FROM item
    WHERE i_manufact_id = 816
),
november_dates AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk, d_year
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_moy = 11
),
item_year_agg AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk,
           nd.d_year,
           SUM(ss.ss_sales_price) AS sum_agg
    FROM store_sales AS ss
    JOIN november_dates AS nd ON nd.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_item_sk IN (SELECT i_item_sk FROM filtered_items)
    GROUP BY ss.ss_item_sk, nd.d_year
)
SELECT iya.d_year,
       fi.i_brand_id AS brand_id,
       fi.i_brand AS brand,
       SUM(iya.sum_agg) AS sum_agg
FROM item_year_agg AS iya
JOIN filtered_items AS fi ON fi.i_item_sk = iya.ss_item_sk
GROUP BY iya.d_year, fi.i_brand, fi.i_brand_id
ORDER BY iya.d_year, SUM(iya.sum_agg) DESC, fi.i_brand_id
LIMIT 100

2. NOVEMBER DATE-MAP MATERIALIZATION — TARGET: the `date_dim` predicate `d_moy = 11` and the `date_dim` to `store_sales` join on `d_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk` — TRANSFORMATION: precompute only the November `(d_date_sk, d_year)` pairs and use them as a compact lookup/semijoin on `store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk`, discarding non-November sales rows before summing.

3. SET-BASED ITEM-YEAR PRE-AGGREGATION — TARGET: the remaining `store_sales` rows after the item and November filters, grouped by `ss_item_sk` and `d_year` — TRANSFORMATION: aggregate `SUM(ss_sales_price)` at `(ss_item_sk, d_year)` granularity in a simple non-correlated derived subquery, collapsing all per-ticket fact rows to one row per item per year before brand attributes are added.

4. FINAL BRAND-YEAR GROUP AND TOP-N — TARGET: the outer `GROUP BY d_year, i_brand_id, i_brand ORDER BY sum_agg DESC LIMIT 100` — TRANSFORMATION: perform the final brand/year grouping, ordering, and limit only on the small item-year preaggregated set, reattaching `i_brand_id` and `i_brand` from the filtered `item` set, so no large fact-table sort or second scan occurs.

5. COLUMN PROJECTION PUSHDOWN — TARGET: the `store_sales` columns `ss_sold_date_sk`, `ss_item_sk`, and `ss_sales_price` — TRANSFORMATION: in the reduced fact scan/subquery, touch only those three columns and never materialize the full `store_sales` row, minimizing I/O from the base fact table.
